ruleCards.title: Direction or location?
ruleCards.rule: Swedish has two words for many places. Use the direction word with movement verbs (gå, åka, komma, springa, flytta): it answers “Vart?”. Use the location word with verbs of being somewhere (vara, bo, sitta, stå, stanna): it answers “Var?”.
ruleCards.watch: The direction word is usually the short one: hem, hit, dit, upp, ner, in, ut, bort.

fun.sv: – Vart ska du? – Ingenstans. – Var är du då? – Hemma, i soffan.
fun.en: “Where are you going?” “Nowhere.” “Where are you, then?” “At home, on the sofa.”

ruleCards.title: Hem or hemma?
ruleCards.rule: Hem is movement towards home. Hemma is being at home.
ruleCards.watch: Stanna means you stay where you are, so it takes the location word: stanna hemma.

fun.sv: Jag är hemma, men hjärnan är kvar på jobbet. Den kommer hem vid åtta.
fun.en: I’m at home, but my brain is still at work. It gets home around eight.

ruleCards.title: Här or hit?
ruleCards.rule: Hit is movement to the place where the speaker is. Här is being in that place.
examples: Vi flyttade hit för två år sedan.
We moved here two years ago.
ruleCards.watch: English says “here” for both. Ask yourself: is someone moving? Then it’s hit.

fun.sv: – Kom hit! – Nej, det är skönt här, säger katten.
fun.en: “Come here!” “No, it’s nice here,” says the cat.

ruleCards.title: Där or dit?
ruleCards.rule: Dit is movement to a place over there. Där is being in that place.
ruleCards.watch: The question words work the same way: Var bor du? (location) but Vart ska du? (direction).

fun.sv: Min syster bor i Spanien. Jag åker dit varje vinter och stannar där så länge jag kan.
fun.en: My sister lives in Spain. I go there every winter and stay there as long as I can.

ruleCards.title: Upp/uppe and ner/nere
ruleCards.rule: Upp and ner are movement up or down. Uppe and nere say where something is.
examples: I go up to the attic.
The cat is up on the roof.
She runs down to the lake.
The children are down by the lake.
ruleCards.watch: Jag går upp klockan sju = I get up at seven. Är du uppe? = Are you up (awake)?

fun.sv: I december går solen upp klockan tio och ner klockan två. Den är inte uppe länge.
fun.en: In December the sun comes up at ten and goes down at two. It isn’t up for long.

ruleCards.title: In/inne and ut/ute
ruleCards.rule: In and ut are movement in or out. Inne and ute say where something is.
ruleCards.watch: Gå ut can also mean going out in the evening: Vi går ut på fredag.

fun.sv: Katten vill gå ut. När den är ute vill den in. När den är inne vill den ut.
fun.en: The cat wants to go out. When it’s out, it wants to come in. When it’s in, it wants to go out.

ruleCards.title: Bort or borta?
ruleCards.rule: Bort is movement away. Borta means away (not here) or gone.
ruleCards.watch: Ska can carry the direction without a movement verb: Jag ska hem. Vart ska du?

fun.sv: Katten tar min socka och springer bort. Nu är sockan borta för alltid.
fun.en: The cat takes my sock and runs away. Now the sock is gone forever.
